content.title: St. Mary's University Admissions 2026 - Requirements, Acceptance Rate & How to Apply
content.text: What is the accreditation of St. Mary's University? St. Mary's University holds accreditation from the Southern Association of Colleges and Schools Commission on Colleges (SACSCOC), which authorizes the institution to award bachelor's, master's, and doctoral degrees. This regional accreditation is a standard marker of academic quality and institutional integrity, recognized nationwide. Additionally, several of the university's individual programs have received specialized accreditation from professional accrediting bodies. These programmatic accreditations further signify that specific courses of study meet rigorous standards set by relevant professional organizations, assuring prospective students of the quality and relevance of their education in those fields. What are the admission requirements at St. Mary's University? Applicants to St. Mary's University must hold a General Educational Development (GED) credential or equivalent high school completion. Submission of a secondary school record and a minimum required GPA are mandatory, while ranking within the graduating class is recommended but not compulsory. The university requests proof of English proficiency through the Test of English as a Foreign Language (TOEFL) for non-native speakers, with other tests also suggested though not strictly required. A computer is necessary for the application process, with options for leasing available. Although standardized admission test scores are not explicitly required, the university recommends submitting other assessments to support the application. Dual credit is not accepted, yet Advanced Placement (AP) credits can be applied toward degree requirements. Open admission is not offered, and a prior college program is advisable to improve admission prospects. St. Mary's University maintains a competitive acceptance rate of 89%, indicating selective admission criteria. Among applicants, approximately 35% submit SAT scores, although detailed distributions are unreported, while about 10% provide ACT scores, with enrolled students mostly scoring below 29 on the ACT. The institution admits a broad range of students but expects demonstration of academic competency, as evidenced by the careful evaluation of secondary school performance and additional recommendations when available. What are the application fees and waivers at St. Mary's University? St. Mary's University requires prospective students to submit an application fee when applying. This fee is a standard component of the admissions process, helping to cover administrative costs associated with reviewing applications. However, the university offers fee waivers under certain circumstances to ensure that financial hardship does not prevent capable applicants from completing their applications. Students who qualify for fee waivers typically include those who demonstrate limited financial resources or who are participating in specific programs that the university recognizes as eligible for a waiver. Details on eligibility criteria and the application process for waivers are available through the university's admissions office or official application portal. Applicants are encouraged to verify the most current fee amounts and waiver policies directly from St. Mary's University to ensure accuracy, as these can vary with each admission cycle. What types of ROTC programs are available at St. Mary's University? St. Mary's University offers a Reserve Officers' Training Corps (ROTC) program directly on its campus, providing students with a structured military training experience alongside their academic studies. This on-campus presence means students can participate in ROTC activities without needing to commute to another institution. Additionally, the university serves as a cooperating host institution for an ROTC branch unit, further expanding opportunities for students interested in pursuing military leadership training during their college years. What are the requirements for transfer students at St. Mary's University? St. Mary's University welcomes transfer students with an open admissions approach, reflecting a noncompetitive entrance difficulty. Prospective transfers can begin their studies during the fall, spring, or summer terms, offering flexibility in enrollment timing. The university accepts transfer credits, including those earned through the Defense Activity for Non-Traditional Education Support (DANTES) program, facilitating a smoother transition for military-affiliated students. Additionally, recommendations are considered as part of the application process, potentially supporting an applicant's candidacy. These policies indicate that St. Mary's University accommodates transfer students with a degree of inclusivity and offers several pathways to integrate previous academic work. What types of study abroad programs are available at St. Mary's University? St. Mary's University offers prospective students a variety of study abroad opportunities designed to enrich their academic and cultural experiences. These programs span multiple disciplines and provide participants with the chance to immerse themselves in international settings while earning academic credit. Students can engage in semester-long exchanges, short-term faculty-led trips, and summer programs, each tailored to different academic schedules and interests. The university collaborates with partner institutions worldwide, facilitating placements in countries across Europe, Latin America, and Asia. Many of the programs emphasize experiential learning, combining classroom instruction with hands-on activities such as internships, service projects, and cultural excursions. This approach allows students to apply theoretical knowledge in real-world contexts while developing a global perspective. Additionally, St. Mary's University supports study abroad through dedicated advising services that help students select suitable programs aligned with their degree requirements and personal goals. Financial aid options and scholarships may be available to assist with program costs, making international study more accessible. Overall, the range of study abroad options at St. Mary's University offers flexibility and academic rigor, catering to diverse interests and timelines among its student body.
